paragraph: Palisades Park is not a single-family town by volume. Only 7 detached homes closed in six months, mostly three-bedroom colonials and bi-levels with two baths, at a median of $780,000, and with a median 60 days on market and a 0.97 sale-to-list ratio, those sellers are okay with waiting for the right buyer rather than pricing to move fast. Two-families are the real story of the local housing stock, with 14 sales at a median of $1,295,000, every one of them a two-family, typically six bedrooms and four baths. That tier moved in about 30 days with roughly a third selling above asking, so competitive but not frenzied. Condos and townhouses carry the volume at 32 sales and a median slightly over a million at $1,014,444, and the typical unit is a three-bedroom, three-bath, which tells you this category is largely newer construction rather than small older apartments. Prices there run from $259,500 to $1,460,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Condo medians have climbed from the mid $600,000s in February into the high six figures and beyond by summer, which tracks the normal seasonal arc, though monthly counts are small enough that mix explains part of it. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the rental income of a two-family, or the low-maintenance newer construction of a condo or townhouse.
